author: fwyzard
body: #### PR description: This PR speeds up the alpaka CA kernels of `RecoTracker/PixelSeeding` on GPUs, mostly by reducing the number of idle threads in the kernels where the work per thread varies a lot from one element to the next. Technical only, the physics results are unchanged. The changes, one per commit: - **Iterative depth-first search in `Kernel_find_ntuplets`**: the recursive `CACell::find_ntuplets` was inlined once per depth (226 registers per thread on CUDA); it now does the same visit with an explicit per-thread stack (55 registers), and saves the ntuplets with the new `CACell::save_ntuplet`. - **Compact the starting cells of `Kernel_find_ntuplets`**: a new `Kernel_select_starts` collects the cells that can start an ntuplet, so that `Kernel_find_ntuplets` runs only over them. - **Balance the work of `Kernel_connect` across threads**: `Kernel_connect` now takes 128 outer cells per block; on GPUs it spreads the (outer cell, candidate inner cell) pairs evenly over the threads of the block, using a prefix sum in shared memory, while on the back-ends with a single thread per block it walks the outer cells in order and loops over their candidates, as before. The triplet dump of the `CA_TRIPLET_DUMP` build is filled by the same kernel, and the previous 2D kernel is removed. - **Go through the whole phi window at once in `GetDoubletsFromHisto`**: the bins of the phi window of an inner hit are contiguous in the `PhiBinner`, so the threads go through the whole window instead of bin by bin. - **Search the ntuplets one depth at a time on GPUs**: one launch of `Kernel_find_ntuplets_level` per depth, each thread expanding one node of the search tree; a node that does not fit in the node storage (one node per cell) is searched depth first, so the result does not depend on the storage size. The level-by-level search is used only by the back-ends with more than one thread per block; the back-ends with a single thread per block (`alpaka::isSingleThreadAcc`, i.e. the serial and TBB CPU back-ends) keep the depth-first search. The other changes apply to all back-ends. Throughput of the Phase-2 NGT tracking (`HLT:75e33_trackingOnly` with `--procModifiers alpaka,ngtScouting`, D128), reading the events with `RepeatingCachedRootSource`, on a pod with 31 cores of a 2 AMD EPYC 9534 machine and one NVIDIA L40S, measured along the commits on `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-25-2300` (average sigma of 4 measurements, in ev/s; the 3 GPU jobs run with NVIDIA MPS; CPU only = serial back-end, `process.options.accelerators = ['cpu']`): | | Commit | GPU, 1 job 24 cores | GPU, 3 jobs 8 cores | CPU only, 1 job 24 cores | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | baseline IB | 192.1 0.2 | 203.2 0.2 | 28.7 0.2 | | 1 | Iterative depth-first search in `Kernel_find_ntuplets` | 200.0 0.1 (+4.1%) | 214.9 0.2 (+5.8%) | 28.8 0.1 (+0.0%) | | 2 | Compact the starting cells of `Kernel_find_ntuplets` | 203.7 0.4 (+6.0%) | 216.1 0.2 (+6.3%) | 29.1 0.1 (+1.1%) | | 3 | Balance the work of `Kernel_connect` across threads | 225.1 0.3 (+17.2%) | 236.4 1.2 (+16.3%) | 30.1 0.4 (+4.6%) | | 4 | Go through the whole phi window at once in `GetDoubletsFromHisto` | 234.0 0.3 (+21.8%) | 245.8 0.3 (+21.0%) | 29.1 0.1 (+1.2%) | | 5 | Search the ntuplets one depth at a time on GPUs | 239.6 0.5 (+24.7%) | 249.9 0.3 (+23.0%) | 29.4 0.1 (+2.4%) | #### PR validation: On `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-25-2300`, for the IB and after each commit: - physics: over 1000 events, the tracks (`hltGeneralTracks`) and pixel vertices (`hltPhase2PixelVertices`) are identical to those of the IB after every commit, both on the GPU (1878301 tracks, 209358 vertices) and with the serial CPU back-end (1878305 tracks, 209359 vertices): same number per event, and identical values of pt, eta, phi, chi2/ndof, number of valid hits, dxy, dz and charge of the tracks, and of the position, ndof, chi2 and number of tracks of the vertices; - throughput: see the table above; - with `CA_TRIPLET_DUMP` enabled, the triplet dump written by the new `Kernel_connect` on the GPU is identical to the one of the IB (56314167 rows over 200 events); on the CPU the triplets and their features are the same, and the in-kernel score differs only by rounding (at most 4 10 relative); - the package builds without warnings, `scram b code-format` gives no changes, and its unit tests pass.
title: Optimise the CA kernels
